reviews.review_msg: I think he's very easy to talk to, and if you negotiate with him, your grade might improve. Be careful the answers for midterms and finals are very rigid. If you don't follow the standard answer, you'll definitely lose points. So always check your exams; you might be able to get some points back.

Very chill prof imo, gave out a lot of late days for the assignments (you will probably need it). Best to focus more on the ppt slides for midterms and finals since quite a bit of what he's going to test is going to be there.

Security requires a solid understanding of programming and protocols. If this course feels very difficult, it may mean security is not the right fit for you, or that you relied too much on AI in previous cmpt courses. LLMs will not help here due to their policy. Exams are tricky, but heavily curved.

As others have noted the content was mostly recycled from a different 403 offering with Android security attached to it, which I found to be just the right amount. Lectures are somewhat boring. Assignments involve some hands on stuff and are pretty fun. Exams include material not covered in lectures but with the curve it wasn't too bad after all.

He extends the course content to include mobile security, so there's a lot of material to cover for the final. His lectures can be dry and he didn't explain concepts very well imo. His exams are not fair at all… a lot of overly specific and unrelated questions. Assignments are really cool but require lots of time and self-teaching.

Exams: Hell on earth

Homework: Actually interesting

Tao Wang's CMPT 403 materials + mobile security from other school, basically 1.5 terms of material in 1 term. Lectures are dry, no practice exam questions, and need at least 50% on exams to pass (midterm avg was 49). Final may included some topics/questions that are not covered in the slides and class.

Lectures were just him reading borrowed slides, often pausing because he didn't understand the material. No exam prep was provided the exams were much harder than the slides. Assignments required implementing Bluetooth protocols with no guidance, you need to figure it out on our own. Avoid if possible, you'll be teaching yourself the entire course.

Exams: Hell on earth

Homework: Actually interesting
